subject: Commitment rollover & invoice smoothing for AWS private offer
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nebulaai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal/commitment amendment question — Nebula PO

Hi Priya,

We're starting prep for our annual renewal and want to align the private offer flow with our fiscal calendar. A couple of asks from procurement and finance:

- Can Redwood smooth our committed units across quarterly invoices (our Q3/Q4 usage spikes)? Ideally we pay four equal tranches but apply any unused committed units to future quarters (rollover).
- If we move to an AWS private offer, how does that affect invoicing — will Redwood still invoice directly or will Marketplace bill us?
- Quick request: can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an amendment PO (same legal entity) instead of re-issuing a brand-new contract?

I attached our last 6-month usage for reference.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Procurement Lead, Nebula AI
[sara.liu@nebulaai.com]
[Attachment: usage-breakdown-q1q2.csv (csv)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nebulaai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal/commitment amendment question — Nebula PO

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and the usage file; this is helpful. High-level answers below, plus a recommended approach so we can move fast: 

1) Commitment smoothing & rollover: we can support quarterly tranche invoicing (4 equal invoices) and allow up to 20% of unused committed units to roll over to the next quarter within the 12-month term. Unused units beyond the 20% cap convert to on-demand usage at the committed rate.

2) Marketplace vs direct invoicing: for AWS private offers customers frequently prefer the marketplace flow for procurement governance; Redwood can initiate an AWS private offer to map the committed capacity to a marketplace SKU. In that case, AWS may show the commitment on the Marketplace invoice while Redwood issues a reconciliation invoice that aligns usage and overage charges. If Nebula prefers a single vendor invoice, we can keep it as a direct PO with Redwood — we just need to confirm your internal approval for a direct invoice.

3) Amendment PO: yes — we can accept an amendment PO referencing the existing contract. We'll need the PO number and finance contact to populate the DocuSign amendment. Please attach the draft PO when available.

Next steps I suggest:
- I will pull an estimated quarter-by-quarter smoothing proposal and share a mutual action plan by EOD tomorrow.
- If you want marketplace flow, let us know by Thu so Marissa can kick off the AWS private offer submission.

Attaching a quick sample amendment template for procurement to use.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
[Attachment: Nebula_PO_Amendment.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks Priya — a couple clarifications from finance: 

- Tax and billing entity: we require Redwood to indicate whether invoices will be issued by Redwood Inc. (US entity) or via AWS Marketplace (which affects VAT/tax handling).
- Invoice schedule: we prefer tranche billing aligned to our fiscal quarters (Jul, Oct, Jan, Apr). If the marketplace invoices have different dates, it creates reconciliation work for us. Can Redwood confirm exact invoice dates for each tranche once the approach is decided?

Also, please include any DocuSign or PO fields that are mandatory on your end (billing address, remit-to, PO line item IDs).

Subject: RE: Renewal/commitment amendment question — Nebula PO

Markus / Sara — quick note on the AWS private offer logistics from Marketplace ops: 

- AWS private offers are usually the cleanest for procurement, but they do create a two-step invoice visibility situation: AWS will surface the commitment, and Redwood issues a recon invoice for true-ups/overages. We can align the invoice dates so your AP team receives predictable dates; typically we request the private offer be created within the same billing month as the first tranche.
- Required fields for DocuSign amendment: PO number, billing address, ECCN (if applicable), and your accounting contact. I'll attach our Marketplace checklist.
- If Nebula prefers Redwood-issued invoices only, we can proceed with a direct PO amendment and skip the AWS private-offer submission. That route is slightly faster from an ops perspective (~5 business days vs ~8-12 for private offer acceptance depending on AWS queue).

I'll have Ben and Jonas stand by to confirm the exact invoice schedule and to generate the DocuSign packet once we have the PO number.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace & Channel, Redwood Inference
